geo.label: Fed lift-off meets a war-risk margin squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

Russia's recognition of the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' and the order to move troops into them turned a slow-burning geopolitical risk into a priced energy and margin shock, just as the Federal Reserve prepares to lift rates. The S&P 500 closed at 4,304.76 index points, -1.01% from the 2022-02-18 close and -2.39% over 20 sessions, while the VIX rose to 28.81 index points, +1.06 points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Reuters described the S&P 500 confirming a correction as stocks stumbled on war fears [[n1924]], and CNBC noted the Dow closing at its lowest level of 2022 so far [[n0711]]. Our stance is Bearish: costs are rising faster than demand, with oil nearing $100 a barrel in The Guardian's framing [[n1263]], and the first sanctions did not remove the escalation tail.
Rates & Curve

The Treasury curve has done much of the Fed's work in advance. The 2Y yield stands at 1.56% and the 10Y at 1.94%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +38 bps, with the 3M bill at 0.37% and the 30Y at 2.24% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22). Over 20 observations the 2Y has risen +57 bps from 0.99% while the 10Y gained only +19 bps from 1.75%, so the spread compressed by 38 bps: a bear flattening (both up, 2Y up more) of a curve that is still positively sloped. The last five observations carry the war signal instead, with the 2Y -2 bps and the 10Y -4 bps, a modest haven bid that has not reversed the policy repricing. Reuters reports the Fed is expected to raise rates 25 bps in March as calls for 50 bps grow louder [[n1820]]; a Fed governor left the door open to a half-point move, Al Jazeera reported [[n1862]], while the New York Fed president saw no need for a 'big' hike, according to China Daily [[n1910]]. The DXY at 96.03 index points, -0.35% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), shows the dollar is not yet acting as the crisis bid.
New / Most Important

President Biden imposed a first tranche of Russia sanctions and called the deployment the 'beginning' of an invasion, Al Jazeera reported [[n1255]]: that is his characterisation of the Donbas move, not a full-scale assault. The domestic transmission runs through energy and margins. Home Depot beat estimates and still sees sales growth ahead, CNBC reported [[n0984]], but Reuters said its margin warning cast a shadow over the quarter [[n0985]], and the shares fell -8.85% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Consumer confidence slid in The Real Economy Blog's latest chart [[n1866]], and a Fed governor predicted sluggish home sales, National Mortgage Professional reported [[n1867]].
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight US equity beta against short-dated Treasuries and energy producers, hedged through index puts rather than outright shorts while the VIX sits at 28.81 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Trigger to add: a further S&P 500 close below 4,304.76 index points together with a 2Y yield pushing above 1.56%, which would confirm the Fed is tightening into a supply shock. What changes the call: a verified Russian de-escalation that pulls Brent back toward the 86.27 USD/bbl of 20 sessions ago, or a Fed signal that March stays at a quarter point, either of which would restore the bid for quality growth.

geo.label: Gas shock tests ECB gradualism
parts: Macro Stance

Europe carries the cleanest exposure to the energy leg of the crisis. Germany halted certification of Nord Stream 2, Spiegel reported [[n1096]], a response The Guardian tied to Russia's recognition of the Ukrainian 'republics' [[n1101]]. Dutch TTF gas jumped +8.17% from the 2022-02-18 close to 79.79 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Equities have so far absorbed the news: the STOXX Europe 600 closed at 455.12 index points, +0.07% on the session, but the DAX is -4.67% over five sessions at 14,693.00 index points. Bearish, because the terms-of-trade hit arrives before any policy cushion.
Activity & Inflation

The pre-shock activity pulse was firm: eurozone growth jumped as virus restrictions eased, the Times of Malta reported [[n1088]]. Prices are the binding constraint. A Reuters poll sees the ECB raising its deposit rate to -0.25% by year-end [[n1044]], while Lagarde repeats a pledge for a gradual policy shift [[n1045]]. In Britain, Reuters reported inflation climbing to 5.5%, the highest since 1992 [[n1064]]. Reuters also noted that European gas storage survived winter but summer refilling looms [[n1081]], which is where a pipeline freeze stops being a symbol and becomes a cost.
New / Most Important

The Nord Stream 2 halt matters less for current flows than for the refill season: the line never delivered gas, but its removal shrinks Europe's options while Russia's Yamal-Europe pipeline flows east, Reuters reported [[n1110]]. The EIA notes three countries provided almost 70% of the LNG Europe received in 2021 [[n1114]], concentrating dependence on seaborne cargoes priced against Asian demand.
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight euro-area cyclicals against the FTSE 100, whose energy and mining weight has it at 7,494.20 index points, +1.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Trigger to extend: TTF holding above 79.79 EUR/MWh as refilling begins. What changes the call: TTF giving back its +8.17% jump on credible non-Russian supply or a pause in escalation, which would let the pre-shock growth momentum reassert itself.

geo.label: Easing central bank, tightening regulators
parts: Macro Stance

China is running two policies at once, and in the latest session the market priced the tighter one. The central bank has eased, with CNBC reporting cuts to key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years [[n0134]], yet Reuters attributed a China tech rout to fresh fears over Beijing's regulatory crackdown [[n0229]]. The Hang Seng fell -2.69% to 23,520.00 index points and the Shanghai Composite -0.96% to 3,457.15 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Our stance on offshore China equity is Bearish: easing is real, but regulation is compressing the profit pool of the index heavyweights, and Russia's isolation adds a sanctions discount.
PMIs & Activity

The latest factory gauge pointed down: Reuters reported January factory activity contracting as COVID lockdowns bit, on the Caixin PMI [[n0144]]. Demand is soft rather than collapsing. Best Selling Cars Blog put January vehicle wholesales up +0.9% in a stable market [[n0220]], and China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved [[n0142]]. Prices leave policy room, with Reuters saying slowing inflation leaves room for easing [[n0154]]. Hong Kong is the near-term activity risk: the BBC reported hospitals overwhelmed amid a spike in cases [[n0165]], and Xi told the city to control its Omicron-fuelled outbreak, Al Jazeera reported [[n0176]].
Credit Impulse

The credit impulse is being pushed from the policy side. Fibre2Fashion reported cuts to rates on medium-term loans and reverse repos [[n0137]], Bloomberg described the central bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0139]], and Al Jazeera reported the central bank chief vowing support amid 'weak links' [[n0162]]. BNP Paribas Asset Management frames the result as US-China monetary policy divergence [[n1142]]. The mechanism matters for markets: cheaper funding lifts credit only where borrowers want to borrow, and with private developers impaired the transmission runs through state firms and infrastructure first, which favours onshore banks and builders over consumer platforms.
Property

Property policy is being loosened at the margin rather than rescued. China excluded affordable rental housing from property credit control, the Khmer Times reported [[n0160]], a targeted carve-out that channels lending to state-sanctioned housing without reopening credit to private developers. Stress keeps surfacing: The Standard reported Fantasia being sued over a bond default [[n0228]]. In Hong Kong, the South China Morning Post argued the Northern Metropolis plan won't affect home prices [[n0224]]. For equities, construction-linked banks and materials remain a funding-cost trade rather than a recovery trade until sales stabilise.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

External friction is rising on several fronts. Reuters reported the US adding e-commerce sites operated by Tencent and Alibaba to its 'notorious markets' list [[n0195]], PBS carried Washington's charge that China's trade policies 'cause serious harm' [[n0174]], and the EU initiated a WTO dispute over Chinese intellectual property enforcement [[n0215]] after imposing anti-dumping tariffs on Chinese steel fasteners, Reuters reported [[n0180]]. The Russia crisis cuts the other way: Reuters reported that as sanctions start, Russia's trade flow is shifting towards China [[n0217]], and the Atlantic Council described the two as partners in de-dollarisation [[n0193]]. That raises secondary-sanctions risk for Chinese lenders and exporters that pick up the slack.
Markets & Flows

Domestic regulation is the swing factor for flows. The WSJ reported that ordered cuts to food-delivery fees sparked a tech selloff [[n0538]], and Bloomberg said the policy wiped $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0539]]. Alibaba's Hong Kong line fell -3.05% to 111.40 HKD and is -15.29% over 20 sessions, Tencent is -5.36% over five sessions at 422.46 HKD, and the KWEB China internet ETF fell -4.24% to 34.09 USD from its 2022-02-18 close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Onshore exposure has held up better, with the ASHR CSI 300 tracker -4.00% over 20 sessions.
New / Most Important

The new information is the reach of supervision. The Japan Times reported Beijing telling banks and state firms to report their exposure to Jack Ma's Ant [[n0219]], which brings financial-sector oversight, not only platform conduct, back into play. The South China Morning Post reported a US$10 million tax-evasion fine on a live-streamer [[n0223]], and the WSJ said Chinese tutoring companies are taking a big financial hit amid the crackdown [[n0222]]. Together these suggest enforcement is broadening across consumer-facing sectors just as investors were testing an easing-led rally.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Hong Kong-listed China internet (KWEB, Alibaba) and express any easing view through onshore exposure such as ASHR at 36.24 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Trigger to revisit: a further policy-rate cut paired with an explicit signal that fee and fintech reviews are complete. What changes the call: the Hang Seng reclaiming 24,952.35 index points, its level 20 sessions ago. ⚠ Divergence: monetary policy is easing and inflation is slowing, which normally supports multiples, yet the regulatory and sanctions discount is widening, so investors are paying for lower rates with lower earnings visibility.

geo.label: Energy-import squeeze, BOJ on hold
parts: Macro Stance

Japan meets the Russia shock as an energy importer with a decelerating factory sector. The Nikkei 225 closed at 26,449.61 index points, -1.71% on the session and -4.13% over 20 sessions, with Tokyo Electron -4.04% and Advantest -4.80% as chip-equipment beta led the decline (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). CNBC reported February factory activity growth falling to a five-month low [[n1316]]. Bearish: the cost shock reaches Japan through the import bill before any offsetting policy response.
Activity & Currency

Trade is the transmission channel. Al Jazeera reported exports growing less than expected as the trade deficit soared [[n1309]], and The Seattle Times earlier reported imports hitting record highs on surging energy prices [[n1286]]. A widening energy deficit weighs on the yen because importers must sell it to pay for fuel, which imports inflation without the wage growth that would let the BOJ respond. Reuters noted a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1300]], a story for later in the year rather than for the next meeting. GDP rebounded before the Omicron wave hit, The Guardian Nigeria reported [[n1298]], so the base is not recessionary. Toyota Motor fell -2.28% to 2,123.50 JPY and Sony Group -2.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
Playbook ✓

Action: underweight Japanese chip-equipment makers against domestic defensives until oil stabilises. Trigger to extend: the Nikkei 225 failing to hold 26,449.61 index points. What changes the call: Brent retreating from 96.84 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) and a rebound in the flash factory gauge, which would revive the reopening trade. Supply-chain localisation, such as TSMC expanding its new Japan chip factory with Denso taking a stake, reported by the Asahi Shimbun [[n1303]], is a multi-year support for the equipment makers, not a near-term catalyst.

geo.label: RBA patient as costs bite
parts: Macro Stance

Australia is a commodity exporter whose central bank refuses to follow the Fed. The WSJ reported the RBA's Harper saying the bank won't follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0045]], even after the AFR reported a shock inflation spike to 3.5 per cent [[n0007]]. The S&P/ASX 200 fell -1.00% to 7,161.30 index points but is +0.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Mixed: export prices support miners and national income, while domestic cost pressure squeezes margins.
Demand & Financing

Corporate results are exposing the cost side. Reuters reported COVID costs hitting Woolworths' profit even as sales soared [[n0067]], and Coles flagged inflation as cost controls limited its H1 profit dip [[n0060]]; the Coles boss told the AFR that higher oil prices and a lack of migration will push up inflation [[n0702]]. Labour is tight, with The Australian reporting the jobless rate at a 13-year low [[n0002]]. On exports, The Australian reported China threatening an iron ore single market [[n0069]], and Fortescue Metals is -10.51% over five sessions at 19.32 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
Playbook ✓

Action: favour diversified and energy-exposed miners over iron-ore pure plays and supermarket margins. Trigger: further Chinese intervention in iron ore trading. What changes the call: an RBA turn toward hiking, which would hit rate-sensitive banks, with Commonwealth Bank of Australia already -2.09% on the session at 96.04 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), or Chinese restocking that lifts the ore price.

geo.label: Frontline risk meets NBP tightening
parts: Macro Stance

Poland is the large EU economy closest to the conflict, and it is pricing that proximity through equities and banks rather than through a disorderly currency. Bankier reported the WIG20 at its lowest since May 2021 amid fear on the equity market [[n1484]], and the iShares MSCI Poland ETF fell -3.51% to 19.53 USD from its 2022-02-18 close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Yet StockWatch described the złoty as keeping its cool [[n1497]]. Inflation is the domestic anchor: Forsal reported GUS putting January inflation at 9.2% [[n1383]], and Rzeczpospolita reported the MPC lifting rates to their highest in almost nine years [[n1378]]. Mixed: the macro base is strong, but the security premium and the inflation fight both weigh on valuations.
Markets

Warsaw's latest session brought a relief bounce led by energy and commodity names: JSW rose +7.96% to 45.18 PLN, PGE +3.97% to 7.49 PLN, KGHM +3.35% to 157.55 PLN and Orlen +2.32% to 69.70 PLN, while the WIG20 total-return tracker gained +0.74% to 36.26 PLN, still -4.74% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). The banks carry the damage, with mBank -11.00%, Bank Pekao -9.35% and PKO Bank Polski -7.34% over five sessions. Business Insider Polska flagged the euro pushing through a closely watched złoty threshold [[n1496]], so the currency is softening at the margin without breaking. Parkiet's analysis of how markets would react to a global armed conflict [[n1401]] frames the bank selling: lenders are the most liquid proxy for both the growth hit and foreign-investor exit.
Fiscal & Politics

The fiscal debate is shifting from tax reform to defence and debt service. Bankier reported the government adopting the draft Homeland Defence Act and asked whether NBP profit will finance the armed forces [[n1516]], while Rzeczpospolita reported the pandemic pushing public spending to a record [[n1509]]. Money.pl warned public debt will rise because of the NBP and grow more costly over time [[n1459]], and said Fitch's rating decision cited high inflation and problems with the European Commission [[n1461]]. Polski Ład still dominates domestic politics: Biznes Wprost reported dismissals over it sweeping through the Finance Ministry [[n1476]], and Next Gazeta reported that Grażyna Ancyparowicz, a critic of the reform, has become an adviser to the NBP president [[n1493]]. On EU money, EUobserver reported Poland edging toward a rule-of-law deal [[n1351]] after Reuters reported the top EU court throwing out the Polish and Hungarian challenge to the conditionality mechanism [[n1342]].
Corporate & Sectors

Company news splits between expansion and governance risk. Allegro is opening its platform to EU countries, Business Insider Polska reported [[n1488]], after StockWatch flagged the shares at new lows [[n1452]]; Allegro bounced +4.97% to 32.75 PLN but is -13.49% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Rynek Kolejowy reported good results at Orlen Unipetrol in the Czech Republic [[n1490]], and StockWatch reported PGE wanting to move its headquarters from Warsaw to Lublin [[n1507]]. In coal, the anti-corruption bureau found irregularities in a 289 mln zł JSW Koks investment, Wyborcza reported [[n1473]], even as JSW is +27.45% over 20 sessions on the energy squeeze. Consumer names are weaker, with Dino Polska -16.67% and LPP -10.19% over 20 sessions, consistent with pressure on real incomes, while Fintek reported BLIK's best year with more than 10 mln active users [[n1426]].
Geopolitics & Security

Security risk has become operational. Rzeczpospolita reported the Foreign Ministry not ruling out evacuating Polish diplomats from Ukraine [[n1491]], and Gazeta Prawna reported the prime minister raising the cyber-threat alert level [[n1481]]. Jarosław Kaczyński said Poland must be secure and Ukraine must be saved, Gazeta reported [[n1494]], and Jerzy Buzek told Rzeczpospolita the country must be prepared for Russian aggression [[n1495]]. Allied hardware is arriving: Reuters reported US Abrams tanks for Poland as the Russia threat mounts [[n1352]], and The National Interest reported additional US F-15s sent to bolster NATO's eastern flank [[n1344]]. Notes From Poland reported a trilateral Ukraine, UK and Poland agreement 'in face of Russian aggression' [[n1348]]. The economic link is energy, with WysokieNapiecie asking what will flow through Baltic Pipe and Yamal a year from now [[n1475]].
New / Most Important

Money.pl's warning that Russia's escalation threatens Ukraine with economic collapse and that the problems will not spare Poland [[n1514]] captures the transmission: trade disruption, refugee pressure and dearer energy imports all land on an economy already running high inflation. Gas pricing is distorting behaviour, with Money.pl reporting firms moving en masse to consumer gas tariffs [[n1467]]. The defence-financing proposal [[n1516]] is the most market-relevant fiscal development, because funding the army from central-bank profit shifts the burden onto the NBP balance sheet during a tightening cycle.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish banks against energy and commodity producers (KGHM, JSW, Orlen), and keep złoty exposure hedged. Trigger to cut further: the WIG20 total-return tracker breaking below 36.26 PLN alongside a weaker złoty. What changes the call: sustained de-escalation that lets lenders re-rate on higher rates, with mBank at 432.20 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) showing a rate tailwind swamped by risk premium, or a rule-of-law deal that unlocks EU funds. ⚠ Divergence: tighter NBP policy and a resilient currency would normally favour Polish banks, yet the banks are the worst performers, because the market prices proximity to the conflict above net-interest-margin gains.
Narrative

Technology is caught between a discount-rate shock and solid fundamentals. XLK closed at 151.03 USD, -0.92% from 2022-02-18 and -2.64% over 20 sessions, holding up better than the Nasdaq 100 at -4.40% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Fortune asked how low tech stocks can fall [[n0648]]; the answer depends on duration, not demand.
Reported

Cisco raised its annual earnings forecast and announced $15 bln in share buybacks, Reuters reported [[n0883]], and the stock is +5.87% over five sessions. Palantir's margins will take a hit from higher spending in its commercial push, Reuters reported [[n0476]], and Palantir Technologies is -20.97% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
EPS Upside Watch

Backlog-driven hardware and networking with pricing power, such as Cisco and Broadcom at +6.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), can keep beating because their multiples are less rate-sensitive. Palo Alto Networks introducing its Cortex XSIAM platform [[n0754]] shows security budgets still expanding.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The conventional view treats war as a tech headwind; the better read is that security software and government data platforms gain, with the CDC tapping Palantir to support COVID-19 drug supply, Reuters reported [[n0698]], while the losers are long-duration names whose valuations need the 10Y to stay at or below 1.94% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22).
Narrative

Communication services is the market's clearest de-rating: XLC is -8.29% over 20 sessions at 66.72 USD, and Meta Platforms (FB) is -34.54% over the same span at 202.08 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Bloomberg reported Meta losing its top-10 ranking by market value amid its worst month ever [[n0464]].
Reported

Facebook Reels expanded to 150 countries as Meta looks to counter TikTok, Deadline reported [[n0978]], and Ad Age said Meta is doubling down with new ad features for creators [[n0992]]. Roku's revenue missed on supply-chain snags and its shares fell 20%, Reuters reported [[n0484]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside requires short video to monetise closer to feed advertising; until Reels earns at parity, the revenue mix dilutes margins. Spotify's Joe Rogan deal, said by NME to be worth $200million [[n0955]], is the content-cost mirror: exclusives lift engagement but also fixed costs.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian point is that 'safe' telecoms are not safe either: AT&T is -9.83% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) even as its 3G network shutdown, flagged by CNN [[n0681]], strips out legacy cost. Value in XLC will come from cost discipline and buybacks, not subscriber growth.
Narrative

Financials are the natural winner of a flattening but positive curve, yet the war has capped them. XLF closed at 39.02 USD, -0.51% from 2022-02-18 but +1.85% over 20 sessions, with JPMorgan Chase +4.77% at 151.87 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Reuters reported Wall Street banks fearing inflation, asset-price deflation, even recession [[n0096]].
Reported

Bank of America's CEO said capital-markets business is down but pipelines are full, Reuters reported [[n0392]], and Goldman Sachs lifted its targets in a bid to win over sceptics [[n0436]]. SoFi agreed to buy banking software firm Technisys for $1.1B, Banking Dive reported [[n0771]], and its shares fell -9.92% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income is the lever: a 2Y yield at 1.56%, +57 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22), lifts asset yields faster than deposit costs. AIG's profit beat on general insurance strength, Reuters reported [[n0881]], shows underwriting pricing power.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Russia sanctions are a compliance and fee story more than a credit story for US banks; the real tail is trading losses if volatility persists. Reuters reported Morgan Stanley's role in the Archegos collapse sped up block-trade probes [[n0302]], a reminder that trading revenue carries conduct risk.
Narrative

Energy is the sector the crisis has repriced fastest. Brent closed at 96.84 USD/bbl, +3.53% from 2022-02-18 and +12.25% over 20 sessions, with WTI at 92.35 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). The New York Times reported oil nearing $100 a barrel as Ukraine developments roiled energy markets [[n1109]].
Reported

Exxon and Papua New Guinea signed a deal to clear the way for the P'nyang gas field, Reuters reported [[n0717]], and Norway's oil firms hiked their 2022 investment plans [[n0471]]. Wood Group shares slid on a $100mn charge and delayed results, the Financial Times reported [[n1003]]: services margins stay fragile even as producers prosper.
EPS Upside Watch

Upstream earnings follow price with a lag, and at these levels free cash flow funds buybacks. Supply discipline supports the margin: Middle East Eye reported Saudi Arabia rejecting a US request to increase oil production [[n1073]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

XLE fell -1.62% to 66.95 USD from 2022-02-18 even as Brent rose (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), so equity holders doubt the price will last. The diplomatic risk is real, with the WSJ reporting the US nearing a return to the Iran nuclear deal [[n1245]], but producers priced for mean reversion are the opportunity.
Narrative

Industrials split between pricing power and input-cost squeeze. XLI closed at 97.39 USD, -4.31% over 20 sessions, with Caterpillar -4.34% and Deere -8.65% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). FreightWaves reported an economist calling freight-rate hikes over the past two years unprecedented [[n1680]].
Reported

Deere aims for a bigger profit as price hikes powered an earnings beat, Reuters reported [[n0543]]. Airbus is pulling away from Boeing with a $4.8 billion record net income, AirGuide Business reported [[n1649]], though the WSJ said its plan to ramp up production of its bestselling jet has hit snags [[n0383]].
EPS Upside Watch

Aerospace and defence carry the upside: Airbus is +5.30% over 20 sessions at 114.08 EUR, General Dynamics +4.70% and Raytheon Technologies (RTX) +6.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). American Airlines plans more schedule cuts while it waits for 787 jet deliveries, Reuters reported [[n0528]], so supply, not demand, still caps volumes.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus reads Deere's beat as a farm-cycle story; with wheat +5.93% from 2022-02-18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), it is a commodity-supply story, yet the stock's -4.15% fall says investors fear peak margins. Labour is the binding constraint, with ABC putting the construction workforce shortage at 650,000 [[n1870]].
Narrative

Consumer discretionary is where the margin squeeze shows first. XLY fell -2.92% to 174.75 USD from 2022-02-18 and Home Depot -8.85% to 316.17 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). CNN noted that Home Depot, the top Dow stock of 2021, is off to a rough start this year [[n0725]].
Reported

Home Depot saw two years of record sales, Business Insider noted [[n0983]], and CNBC said bigger orders from home professionals are key to its growth strategy [[n0994]]. Macy's earnings topped estimates and it won't spin off e-commerce, CNBC reported [[n0989]]. Tesla faces a US investigation of 416,000 vehicles over unexpected braking, Reuters reported [[n1673]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside sits where demand is reopening-driven rather than goods-driven: Airbnb beat and gave strong guidance, CNBC reported [[n0871]], and is +11.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Carvana's plan to add 3,500 jobs in Atlanta, Automotive News reported [[n0700]], contrasts with its -24.48% fall.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Revenue beats are being sold when margins slip, so Reuters' warning that cooling home-improvement demand may pressure Home Depot and Lowe's 2022 sales [[n0965]] matters more for guidance than for the top line. Lowe's at 214.59 USD, -3.64% from 2022-02-18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), is already discounting it.
Narrative

Staples are the relative haven: XLP is +0.53% over five sessions at 75.44 USD against -2.20% for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). The question is whether pricing power outlasts a new commodity shock from the Black Sea.
Reported

Walmart profits grew as consumers continued to spend, The New York Times reported [[n0508]], although CNBC said Walmart shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0509]]. Kraft Heinz packed an earnings beat on raised prices, ET Retail reported [[n0457]], and Nestlé is confident cost inflation won't take a bite out of margins, Reuters reported [[n0466]].
EPS Upside Watch

Coca-Cola is +3.87% over 20 sessions at 62.28 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). London-listed Coca-Cola HBC is readying Russia contingencies as profits rise, Reuters reported [[n0741]], a direct test of how European bottlers ring-fence Russian earnings.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The pricing-power trade has a political ceiling: Fortune reported Bernie Sanders slamming corporations for raising prices despite record profits [[n0973]], and Reuters described hard bargains as European retailers take on food giants [[n0433]]. Grain inflation could trap manufacturers between suppliers and retailers.
Narrative

Health care's steady cash flows make it a funding source rather than a winner. XLV is -1.43% over 20 sessions at 127.19 USD while AbbVie is +10.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Moderna's CEO said it is 'reasonable' to think the pandemic may be in its final stages, CNBC reported [[n0296]], which is why vaccine makers lag.
Reported

Bayer hiked Nubeqa's peak-sales goal to more than €3B on prostate cancer data, Fierce Pharma reported [[n0923]], and Bristol Myers won FDA priority review for its Breyanzi expansion [[n0924]]. Sanofi and Regeneron ditched a Dupixent trial in hives, Fierce Pharma reported [[n0583]].
EPS Upside Watch

Novartis' Leqvio could reap $2.5B by 2027, an analyst told Fierce Pharma [[n0749]]: durable franchises with pricing power are being valued over COVID revenue, with Moderna -7.84% and Pfizer -7.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Biotech is not a defensive. XBI is -3.72% over 20 sessions at 88.68 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), and STAT reported some newly public biotechs trading below cash [[n1543]], a sign funding risk, not science, is the constraint. Managed care is the cleaner hedge.
Narrative

Materials are the supply-shock beneficiaries. Alcoa is +27.70% over 20 sessions at 74.09 USD, aluminium futures stand at 3,342.00 USD/t, and Mosaic is +12.99% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Reuters warned commodity supplies are at risk if Russia is hit by sanctions [[n0541]].
Reported

DuPont will shed its mobility and materials unit in an $11 bln Celanese deal, Reuters reported [[n0549]]. Barrick declared an increased dividend and a performance dividend policy [[n0246]], and Glencore reported record earnings while setting aside $1.5 billion for probes, Reuters reported [[n0876]].
EPS Upside Watch

Nickel prices soared on Russia tension and tight supply, Macau Business reported [[n1700]], and palladium is +10.87% over 20 sessions at 2,369.30 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Trade Data Monitor notes Ukraine is a key iron ore and metals supplier [[n0071]], so disruption tightens several markets at once.
⚡ Breaking Convention

XLB itself is -1.69% over 20 sessions at 82.67 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) because chemical makers buy the inputs that miners sell; the winners are producers of scarce metals and nutrients, not processors. Alcoa's -5.26% drop from 2022-02-18 shows how violent positioning reversals can be.
Narrative

Real estate is a rates trade first: XLRE is -5.17% over 20 sessions at 44.56 USD as the 10Y yield rose +19 bps to 1.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22). Realtor.com reported mortgage rates hitting their highest point since May 2019 [[n1843]].
Reported

Blackstone is buying a multifamily REIT in a $5.8B deal, The Real Deal reported [[n0250]], and Bloomberg said Wall Street is buying starter homes to quietly become America's landlord [[n0198]]. Existing home sales accelerated as investors elbowed out first-time buyers, Reuters reported [[n1857]].
EPS Upside Watch

Landlords retain pricing power: the Joint Center for Housing Studies reported rents soaring, though home prices grew even faster [[n0481]]. Housing permits reaching a 15-year high, per The Real Economy Blog [[n1836]], argue that supply is catching up.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Private capital is bidding for assets that listed REITs are being sold down for, and that gap between take-private appetite and XLRE's drawdown is the opportunity. The risk is cost: new-home construction fell 4.1%, The Guam Daily Post reported [[n1858]].
Narrative

Utilities are failing as a haven because they are bond proxies in a rising-yield market. XLU is -2.98% over 20 sessions at 66.15 USD and NextEra Energy -9.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Fuel costs are a pass-through risk, with Henry Hub gas at 4.50 USD/MMBtu, +11.70% over 20 sessions.
Reported

Duke Energy is eyeing a coal phase-out by 2035, POWER Magazine reported [[n0421]], while WABE reported the $30B Georgia Power nuclear plant delayed up to 6 more months [[n0364]], a cost overhang for its parent.
EPS Upside Watch

Southern Company's CEO said hybrid work is driving residential energy demand, CNBC reported [[n0445]], which supports volumes; Southern Company rose +0.82% from 2022-02-18 to 64.29 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Europe is the warning: EDF needed $2 bln of state help over nuclear outages, Reuters reported [[n0551]]. Regulated US utilities pass fuel costs through, but politics limits the speed, and renewable developers such as NextEra are the long-duration exposure that rising yields punish hardest.
Narrative

European autos are trading corporate action against supply risk. The STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts tracker rose +0.69% to 60.13 EUR but is -3.91% over five sessions, while Volkswagen preference shares jumped +7.84% to 188.70 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) as Reuters reported Volkswagen and its top investor steering towards a Porsche IPO [[n0786]].
Reported

Mercedes-Benz foresees EV-only production lines within a few years, Reuters reported [[n0654]], and Volkswagen expects the chip shortage to ease later in 2022 [[n1643]]. Obserwator Gospodarczy noted German car production still falling, 40% below its level three years ago [[n1382]].
EPS Upside Watch

Mercedes-Benz Group is +6.39% over 20 sessions at 73.22 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22): pricing on constrained volume has protected margins, and easing chip supply would add volume to a strong order book.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The WSJ argues Volkswagen's Porsche IPO won't put investors first [[n1734]], so the listing serves group capital more than minorities. Renault fell -3.76% to 33.57 EUR on the session and BMW is -4.21% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), so the rally is narrow.
Narrative

Semiconductors are holding up on fundamentals: SOXX closed at 463.73 USD, -2.99% over 20 sessions, better than the Nasdaq 100, and Micron is +9.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Nvidia forecast upbeat current-quarter revenue, Al Jazeera reported [[n1623]].
Reported

Nvidia announced its fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0081]], and TechSpot reported it spent $10 billion for a chunk of TSMC's 5nm capacity [[n1701]]. Intel announced its 18A node, TechPowerUp reported [[n1682]], while Notebookcheck reported AMD overtaking Intel's market cap for the first time after the Xilinx merger [[n0241]].
EPS Upside Watch

ASML at 640.27 USD and TSMC at 116.91 USD are -6.86% and -7.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), but capacity spending continues, with Bosch investing $296M to produce semiconductors, TechCrunch reported [[n1733]]; equipment orders rest on that capex.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The Asian equipment selloff, with Tokyo Electron -4.04% and Advantest -4.80%, prices a cyclical top even as SK Hynix is +5.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Reuters reported Taiwan boosting protection for its semiconductor secrets with an eye on China [[n0333]]: the geopolitical premium now attaches to fabs too.

earnings_pattern.title: Margins, not beats, set the price
parts: Rewarded

Companies that showed pricing power or reopening demand were paid. DoorDash surged more than 30% on record-high order numbers, The Japan Times reported [[n0419]]; CNBC said Cisco defied the doubters with a beat and raise [[n0895]]; Bloomberg reported Kering shares surging as Gucci sales rebounded on a new collection [[n0454]]; and Kraft Heinz's price-driven beat showed staples can pass costs on.
Punished

Pandemic winners whose boost is fading were sold hard. Roblox shares closed down 26% after an earnings miss, CNBC reported [[n0322]]; Shopify closed down 16% after warning its pandemic boost will fade [[n0329]]; and ViacomCBS shares tumbled nearly 20% after its Paramount rebrand and streaming outlook, Deadline reported [[n0347]]. Home Depot's beat came with a margin warning [[n0985]] and a -8.85% fall (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
Pattern

Investors are discounting forward margins rather than trailing revenue. Price-driven beats earn a premium only when management convinces that prices will stick: Deere's price hikes powered a beat [[n0543]], yet the stock is -8.65% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) because investors doubt next year's margin. The same logic hit Roku, whose revenue missed on supply-chain snags, as The Ankler noted the stock falling -26% as revenue growth slows [[n0578]]. Volume growth without margin is not enough in a rising-rate market.
Attention into EPS

The next tests are retailers and discretionary names. Reuters flagged cooling home-improvement demand that may pressure Lowe's 2022 sales [[n0965]], and off-price peers such as TJX Companies are -4.03% over five sessions at 65.25 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), already pricing a softer consumer. Macy's beat and its decision not to spin off e-commerce, Retail Dive reported [[n0990]], set the bar for department stores, while Lucid Group is -32.42% over 20 sessions at 25.51 USD, showing how unforgiving the market is toward cash-consuming growth.
Playbook

Own companies with demonstrated pricing power and low input intensity, such as Cisco and Kering, into results, and fade beats that arrive with margin warnings. Trigger: a gross-margin guide-down is a sell signal even with a revenue beat. What changes the call: an oil retreat that lowers freight and input costs, which would let margin-warning names such as Home Depot recover.

underowned.title: Fertiliser and grain: the Black Sea food chain
parts: Attention Gap

While attention sits on oil, Reuters reported that deepening Russia-Ukraine tensions are seen curbing food supplies and lifting prices [[n0705]]. Wheat rose +5.93% to 844.25 US cents/bu and corn +3.13% to 674.75 US cents/bu from 2022-02-18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
Exposure & Risk

CF Industries (+8.00% over 20 sessions), Mosaic and Nutrien are the equity routes (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), and Farm Policy News flagged ripple effects reaching fertilizer [[n1723]]. The risk is a sharp reversal in grain futures on any de-escalation, or political caps on food prices.
Trigger to Watch

Confirmation would come from physical disruption of Black Sea grain trade; Marketplace reported the conflict could push grain prices higher worldwide [[n1724]]. Wheat holding above 844.25 US cents/bu would keep the theme alive.

underowned.title: Non-Russian gas: US supply into Europe's refill
parts: Attention Gap

Henry Hub gas at 4.50 USD/MMBtu is +11.70% over 20 sessions while Dutch TTF at 79.79 EUR/MWh is -14.21% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22): Europe's refill problem is priced in Rotterdam, not in US producers.
Exposure & Risk

The EIA forecasts US marketed natural gas production rising in 2022 and 2023 [[n1674]], and Brookings argued now is not the time to limit US natural gas exports [[n1083]]. Exposure runs through US gas producers within XLE; the risks are a mild spring and export-capacity limits.
Trigger to Watch
CNN's description of Nord Stream 2 as on the scrap heap [[n1113]] becomes investable if the freeze persists into the refill season and Europe signs longer seaborne contracts.

underowned.title: Russia-sensitive metals: aluminium, palladium, nickel
parts: Attention Gap

Aluminium at 3,342.00 USD/t is +10.83% and palladium +10.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), yet attention is fixed on crude. Commodity supply is the sanctions channel that markets have only begun to price.
Exposure & Risk

Alcoa, +27.70% over 20 sessions, and platinum-group producers are the levered expressions; Macau Business reported nickel soaring on Russia tension and tight supply [[n1700]]. The risk is that sanctions spare metals, as the UK spared Russia's top banks: Reuters reported Sberbank and VTB shares rebounding as they escaped UK sanctions [[n0764]].
Trigger to Watch
Any Western measure naming Russian metal producers or restricting their exports, which would turn a premium into physical shortage.

underowned.title: European defence: from budget line to priority
parts: Attention Gap

Rheinmetall is +6.23% over 20 sessions at 95.90 EUR and +2.20% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), while Reuters reported Airbus reviewing its defence business as pressures mount [[n0267]]. European defence is still treated as a niche.
Exposure & Risk

The International Centre for Defence and Security wrote that the Baltic states would wish Germany's new government to step up in defence [[n1084]]. Exposure is Rheinmetall and Airbus; the risk is that budgets move slowly and procurement favours US primes, with ITA -0.06% over 20 sessions.
Trigger to Watch
A formal German or EU commitment to higher defence outlays, which would convert rhetoric into multi-year order books.

crypto.title: Bitcoin bounces, crypto equities do not
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed its last UTC day at 38,286.03 USD, +3.27% on the day but -5.56% over five days, and Ether at 2,639.30 USD, +2.54% and -8.40% over five days, while Solana is -15.09% over 20 days at 86.47 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-22). The equity wrappers trade on US sessions and absorbed the full shock: Coinbase Global fell -6.56% to 176.76 USD, MicroStrategy -4.61% and GBTC -5.02% from 2022-02-18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Crypto is trading as high-beta risk, not as a sanctions hedge.
New / Most Important

Ethereum founder Vitalik Buterin said crypto 'welcomes' another winter, Bloomberg reported [[n0832]], while the Financial Stability Board warned of emerging risks from crypto-assets to global financial stability [[n0808]]. Capital still arrives at the venture layer: Sequoia launched a $500 million fund to invest in crypto tokens, Forbes reported [[n0821]], and stablecoin firm Circle doubled its valuation to $9 billion in a new SPAC deal, Ledger Insights reported [[n1134]]. Marketing is on the defensive, with Business Insider reporting Coinbase backpedalling over its Super Bowl ad controversy [[n0126]], and CoinGeek reported the FCA concerned about Binance's backdoor re-entry into the UK payments network [[n0838]].
Playbook

Action: treat Bitcoin as a liquidity asset and prefer it over leveraged miners and exchange equities, where Iris Energy's +52.09% 20-session run (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) marks the most crowded position. Trigger: a Bitcoin close back below 36,952.98 USD, its level 20 days ago (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-22), would confirm that risk-off is winning. What changes the call: Bitcoin holding its bounce while the VIX falls back from 28.81 index points, which would signal genuine decoupling from equities.

flows.title: Liquidity tightens before the war premium is paid
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is being withdrawn on two fronts: the Fed's lift-off and balance-sheet run-off, and a risk premium that is closing some issuance windows. Reuters examined what could drive the Fed to a 'Plan B' for balance sheet reduction [[n1135]], and Capital Economics argued 'we need to talk about QT' [[n1091]]. Reuters reported global companies slowing debt-raising as yields climb [[n1122]], and Riviera reported deteriorating market conditions forcing Fred Olsen Windcarrier to put its IPO on hold [[n1147]]. Large deals still clear: Reuters reported a Porsche IPO drawing closer after Volkswagen talks [[n0231]], and said India's LIC is set to launch an $8 bln IPO on March 11 [[n1677]].
Rates & Dollar

Short rates are doing the tightening: the 2Y at 1.56% is +57 bps over 20 observations against +19 bps for the 10Y at 1.94% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22). Reuters reported the eurodollar futures market betting that a hawkish Fed could ease rates, slightly, in 2024 [[n1080]], so the market prices a short, sharp cycle. The DXY at 96.03 index points is +0.11% over 20 sessions and -0.35% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22): the dollar is not absorbing haven demand, which keeps pressure off emerging-market funding for now. Gold has taken that role at 1,907.40 USD/oz, +2.03% over five sessions.
Credit Check

Credit is weakening in an orderly way. HYG is -3.10% and LQD -3.88% over 20 sessions, and EMB fell -1.26% to 101.70 USD from 2022-02-18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Investment grade lagging high yield over 20 sessions says this is still a duration problem more than a default problem. The first sanctions were calibrated to avoid a funding accident: the UK statement targeted oligarchs and banks [[n1272]], and The New York Times reported stocks hitting correction territory as governments announced sanctions against Russia [[n0772]], not a credit event. The Standard's report of Fantasia being sued over a bond default [[n0228]] is a reminder that Asian high yield remains the weakest link.
Equity & Fund Flows

Positioning is visible in leverage and corporate action. Wolf Street reported margin debt plunging as stocks tumbled, though leverage is still gigantic [[n1140]]. Companies are buyers: Builders FirstSource approved a $1B stock buyback plan [[n1146]]. Private capital is active, with KKR acquiring a majority stake in Refresco [[n0737]] and Deadline reporting Tegna sold to Standard General and Apollo Global [[n0694]]. City AM reported Berkshire Hathaway dumping Visa and Mastercard stock and buying $1bn of the bitcoin-friendly fintech Nubank [[n0353]], while Business Insider reported Warren Buffett avoiding Russia after threats of violence and asset seizure [[n0790]]. London Stock Exchange's purchase of TORA, which The TRADE put at $325 million [[n0850]], shows exchanges buying trading technology while volatility pays.
Portfolio Implication

Hold quality duration in the belly of the curve, where IEF is -1.40% over 20 sessions while TLT has gained +1.51% over five sessions as a haven (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), and fund it from long-duration equity. Keep gold over dollar cash while the DXY stays near 96.03 index points. Trigger: HYG breaking below 82.70 USD would mark the shift from duration stress to credit stress and justify cutting high-yield exposure. What changes the call: a de-escalation that reopens the IPO window and lifts credit with equities.

anticipatory.title: Sanctions escalation: the next tranche
parts: What Is Priced

Markets have priced a contained first round. Gibson Dunn summarised US and allied sanctions on Russia and the separatist regions [[n1273]], and the BBC reported Germany halting the pipeline as nations sanctioned Russia [[n1118]]. Brent at 96.84 USD/bbl and the VIX at 28.81 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22) price a supply premium, not a financial-system shock.
Conditional Expression

If the next round reaches Russia's largest banks or energy payments, own Brent call spreads and gold and underweight European banks, with Societe Generale already -8.91% over five sessions at 31.42 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). If measures stay aimed at individuals and state-linked companies, sell VIX upside and add back European cyclicals.
Risk

Moscow's response is the unpriced leg: Sky News reported foreign minister Sergei Lavrov saying Russia will retaliate if the UK imposes new sanctions [[n1175]]. Retaliation through gas flows would hit Europe before the US, and a summit, which Biden agreed in principle to hold if Russia did not invade, BBC reported [[n1247]], now looks remote.

anticipatory.title: Fed lift-off: a quarter point or a half
parts: What Is Priced

A March lift-off is consensus; the debate is size. Reuters reported the Fed set to raise 25 bps in March as calls for 50 bps grow louder [[n1820]], and the readout of the January meeting showed the Fed not wed to a particular pace of hikes [[n1896]]. The 2Y at 1.56% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22) sits above the 1.17% 1Y, pricing a steady sequence.
Conditional Expression

If the Fed chooses a half point, the 2Y reprices through 1.56% and bear flattening extends, favouring banks over long-duration tech. If it delivers a quarter point and cites war uncertainty, the 10Y-2Y spread at +38 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22) can re-steepen, and quality growth recovers.
Risk

Bullard again called for a front-loaded rate-rise campaign, the WSJ reported [[n1128]]; an oil-driven inflation surprise would push the Fed toward speed even as growth slows, the combination that compresses equity multiples hardest.

anticipatory.title: Oil near $100: Iran and OPEC+ as the release valve
parts: What Is Priced

NPR reported oil prices surging toward $100 a barrel [[n1264]], and Brent at 96.84 USD/bbl is +12.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). The premium assumes no new supply arrives quickly.
Conditional Expression

Reuters reported the US in the 'very final stages' of Iran nuclear talks [[n1171]], and Reuters reported Asian refiners eager to resume Iranian oil imports as high prices bite [[n1650]]. If a deal is signed, rotate from upstream producers into refiners and airlines; if talks stall, hold XLE and add on dips.
Risk

OPEC+ insists it will continue to maintain balance in oil markets [[n0122]], which can mean either restraint or more barrels. A Russian supply disruption would overwhelm any Iranian volume, so upstream shorts are dangerous until both outcomes are visible.

anticipatory.title: Truth Social and the DWAC premium
parts: What Is Priced

Digital World Acquisition (DWAC) rose +10.18% to 92.90 USD from 2022-02-18 and is +38.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), after Reuters reported the Trump-linked SPAC's shares surging as Truth Social topped Apple downloads [[n0780]]. The price assumes the app scales into a durable platform.
Conditional Expression

The Guardian reported Nunes saying Truth Social will be fully operational by the end of March [[n1576]]. If rollout clears the waitlist, momentum can extend; if errors persist, puts or avoidance are the expression, given SPAC dilution mechanics.
Risk

The Week reported the app crashing for 13 hours immediately after launch [[n1609]], while Reuters, citing Apptopia, put downloads at 170k [[n1604]]. Engagement after the first rush, not downloads, decides whether the premium survives; a SPAC trading on attention can lose it quickly.

catalysts.title: Home Depot (HD)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Home Depot is the test case for margin-led punishment. Business Insider noted it saw two years of record sales [[n0983]], but the stock fell -8.85% to 316.17 USD from 2022-02-18 and is -13.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). The thesis: pro demand holds, yet cost inflation and a cooling DIY customer compress margins.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is the 363.81 USD close of 20 sessions ago, which needs a margin reset to reclaim. Risk to the bearish view: CNBC reported that winning bigger orders from home professionals is key to its growth strategy [[n0994]], a mix shift that could protect sales.
Trade Expression
Underweight against staples and energy; cover if the shares stabilise while lumber and freight costs fall, the sign that margin pressure is peaking.

catalysts.title: Meta Platforms (FB)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The WSJ reported Facebook escalating its TikTok rivalry by launching Reels globally [[n0744]], and TechCrunch said the rollout comes with new creative tools and ads [[n0979]]. The thesis is that a cheaper stock already discounts slower feed growth, while Reels monetisation is the swing.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Meta Platforms (FB) is at 202.08 USD, -34.54% over 20 sessions and -7.18% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Risks: Reuters reported a D.C. prosecutor pressing to question the CEO in a privacy lawsuit [[n0704]], and the WSJ described a costly breakup with advertisers [[n0952]].
Trade Expression
Build a position slowly with options rather than outright stock; add only once advertising pricing on Reels is evidenced and the shares hold 202.08 USD through the next market drawdown.

catalysts.title: Exxon Mobil (XOM)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Exxon combines oil leverage with long-cycle gas growth: Reuters reported Exxon and PNG signing a deal to clear the way for the P'nyang gas field [[n0717]], and Texas refinery workers ratifying an Exxon labour contract offer [[n0776]], which removes an operating risk.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares are at 76.46 USD, +5.04% over 20 sessions but -1.16% from 2022-02-18 while Brent rose +3.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), so the stock lags the commodity. The risk is an Iran deal or de-escalation that collapses the premium.
Trade Expression
Own XOM against a short in long-duration growth; add on a Brent close above 96.84 USD/bbl and cut if Brent falls back toward 86.27 USD/bbl.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Alibaba faces regulatory pressure on two continents. Barron's reported Alibaba and Tencent e-commerce sites added to a US counterfeit and piracy list [[n0189]], and The Japan Times reported Beijing asking banks to report Ant exposure [[n0219]]. Diversification such as rewarding NFTs in its first blockchain game, Yahoo Finance reported [[n0687]], does not offset that.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The ADR fell -5.09% to 112.93 USD from 2022-02-18, and the Hong Kong line is at 111.40 HKD, -15.29% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Risk: a policy pivot toward platform support could spark a violent short-covering rally.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; reassess only if the stock reclaims 120.37 USD, its level 20 sessions ago, on an explicit regulatory all-clear.

catalysts.title: Raytheon Technologies (RTX)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Defence demand is rising as Washington moves forces: the Department of Defense reported Biden shifting US troops in Europe to defend frontline NATO states [[n1254]]. Reuters reported Beijing sanctioning Lockheed and Raytheon again over Taiwan arms sales [[n0639]], a headline cost that matters little to US order books.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Raytheon Technologies (RTX) is at 93.54 USD, +6.15% over 20 sessions, against -2.39% for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22). Risk: its civil aerospace half remains exposed to airline capacity and supply-chain delays.
Trade Expression
Own RTX alongside Lockheed Martin, +3.45% over 20 sessions, as a hedge for escalation; trim if a verified de-escalation removes the urgency of NATO procurement.

catalysts.title: Volkswagen (VOW3.DE)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

A Porsche listing would crystallise value inside the group: Times of Malta reported Volkswagen eyeing a separate stock market listing for Porsche [[n0787]], and Daily Sabah reported the plan for a separate listing [[n0788]]. Volkswagen preference shares jumped +7.84% to 188.70 EUR on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22).
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares are +5.86% over 20 sessions; holding 188.70 EUR is the test that the sum-of-the-parts rerating is real. Risks: chip and energy supply, and the governance concern that the deal serves the family holding more than minorities.
Trade Expression
Own VW preference shares against the STOXX autos tracker at 60.13 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22), isolating the IPO catalyst from sector supply risk; exit if IPO terms disappoint.
